profile.behavior: An almost continuously aerial insectivore; flies rapidly with stiff, shallow wingbeats and clings rather than perches when at rest.
field_marks: Very long, narrow, strongly curved wings
Short, tapered tail with stiff, bristle-like tips
Dark gray-brown overall, with a slightly paler throat
Tiny feet; clings to vertical surfaces rather than perching
Very short, broad-based bill that is often hard to see
profile.habitat: Open airspace over a wide variety of terrain where flying insects are available; nests and roosts on enclosed vertical surfaces, including chimneys, cavities, caves, and similar structures.

sources.title: Chimney Swift Identification — All About Birds

findings: Identity is consistent with Chimney Swift: the plate shows the characteristic sooty gray-brown plumage, subtly paler throat, rounded head, large dark eye, compact cigar-shaped body, long folded wings, short central tail, and vertical-clinging posture seen in the references.

The primary specimen has one head and bill, two anatomically coherent folded wings, two attached legs with gripping feet, and one tail. The far-side structures are convincing for the pose; the detached wing and head are clearly supplementary studies.
The bill is short and broad-based relative to the head in both depicted heads. The feet and sharply curved claws plausibly engage the vertical surface.

All visible identification, habitat, behavior, and field-mark text is complete, legible, correctly ordered, and matches the proposed profile without duplicated, omitted, substituted, or nonsensical wording.

Length 4.7–5.9 in (12–15 cm), weight 0.6–1.1 oz (17–30 g), and wingspan 10.6–11.8 in (27–30 cm) match the Cornell identification page. Audubon publishes a somewhat broader wingspan range, but the plate's value remains directly supported rather than erroneous.

The schematic body-length diagram increases correctly from 4.7 in (12 cm) at the bottom to 5.9 in (15 cm) at the top, repeats the correct range, uses consistent units, and is explicitly labeled NOT TO SCALE.
